dimensions.summary: Compatibility is an isolated public subpath backed by manifest-generated contracts and canonical documentation.
Supported versions are explicit, frozen and registry-backed; compatibility-only types do not collide with the current public type barrel.
Shared ESM chunks reduce packed size while gates measure full transitive browser bundles instead of entry stubs.
Resource inspection precedes version access; accessors, invalid previous contracts and unknown versions fail closed.
Negotiation performs no filesystem, network, telemetry or credential access and emits no local paths.
Browser-neutral ESM and installed package execution pass locally; Linux, macOS and Windows CI evidence remains pending.
Shared retains zero runtime dependencies and no central CLI runtime bridge was added.
Current input is exact; previous input migrates deterministically and the migrated result is revalidated against the current contract.
One supported previous version has forward-only migration with explicit migration/loss records and opaque extension preservation.
Invalid, missing and unsupported version states return stable discriminated results without throwing or guessing migrations.
Frozen fixtures, generated bindings, compatibility policy and consumer tests are separated and traceable.
The real tarball imports compatibility and migrates a shipped fixture locally; remote provenance and publication admission remain pending.

checks.evidence: 10 files and 78 tests passed with generation, types, lint, format, coverage, build, transitive size and packed-consumer gates.
Installed tarball imported /compatibility and migrated the shipped previous fixture with zero runtime dependencies.
Linux, macOS and Windows CI execution is required before admission.
